name: Spark Plugin
description: A plugin that adds 100+ code-free customisations inside the Squarespace editor (mega menus, animations, galleries, popups, hover effects). 14-day free trial (company-stated). The Reddit post doesn't name the product. The poster is u/Rasmusi, describes a Squarespace drag-and-drop customisation tool started ~5 years ago with four part-time freelancers; Spark Plugin's About page lists founder Rasmus Myhrberg, founded 2021, run with an "international team of freelancers". Strong match, but inferred.

mentions.evidence: $400K ARR, bootstrapped, no investors, no full-time employees (founder and 4 part-time freelancers). Self-reported on Reddit, 20 October 2026. The post does not name the product.
mentions.indieAngle: Same play on a platform Polish SMBs actually use and can't customise: Shoper/IdoSell storefront add-ons, or Wix/Framer section packs sold as a subscription plugin.

whyItPrints: Squarespace users hit the limits of the template, search for a fix, and pay monthly. The first 10 customers came from answering questions on the Squarespace forum. Search was the main channel from 2021 to 2024 (self-reported).
whyThisMatters:
Squarespace sites run out of room in the template. This plugin adds menus, galleries, popups, and hover effects inside the editor, without writing code. There is a two-week trial.

A Reddit post on 20 October 2026 describes a Squarespace customisation tool, bootstrapped, with the founder and four part-time freelancers, and a yearly number. The post does not name the product. The poster is u/Rasmusi. Spark Plugin's about page names Rasmus Myhrberg, says the company started in 2021, and says it runs with freelance help. That is a strong match. I am not calling it certain. The first customers, in the post, came from answering questions on the Squarespace forum. Search was the main way people found it for a few years.

You pay so the template can do the thing it would not do on its own.
